text:
Kevin R: Heads-up — spotted a regression in continuous-batching + KV cache when serving mixed long/short contexts. Memory climbs steadily on a small subset of requests, and a few worker threads hit HOL (head-of-line) while others idle. Repro attached in my perf repro gist.

Maria L: ugh, seen this pattern before. Is it the pager thrashing or frag reuse mismatch?

Kevin R: Looks like page-level fragmentation + our batch-merge heuristic. When two batches merge and one has a long ctx, we keep a large KV slice pinned. Then short requests that should reuse freed slots get blocked waiting on the merge path.

Josh P: Can you paste the pprof snapshot? also what kernel selection? i.e., fp16 vs int8 kernels?

Kevin R: pprof snapshot + flame graph: 
```
(pprof) top10
  30.2%  runtime               kv_pager::read_slice
  18.7%  runtime               batch::merge_wait
  12.1%  runtime               kv_cache::fragment_lookup
  8.4%   runtime               scheduler::route_request
```
Also trying both kernels — behavior exists on both fp16 and q4_0, so not kernel-specific.

Tara S: Re: merge_wait — is that our continuous-batch combine path where we serialise head block to maintain cache invariants? Could be HOL from a global mutex.

Kevin R: Yes. The merge path serialises to avoid double-free of slices during staggered eviction. But with long contexts the slice retention time grows and the merge becomes the critical path.

Maria L: What does eviction look like? Are we doing LRU at the per-shard level? Could shards be uneven (hot shards) so one shard holds lots of fragments and causes blocking?

Kevin R: Eviction: per-shard LRU with a global reclaim signal. Hot shards definitely occur — we saw one shard holding ~70% of active slices in the trace. When batch merge touches that shard it tries to coalesce fragments and ends up scanning a long chain.

Josh P: Repro commands you ran? I can run locally.

Kevin R: repro steps (short):
```
# spawn mixed traffic
./bin/perf-client --profile mixed_long_short --qps 400 --long-p50 12000 --short-p50 8 --duration 600
# collect mem + pprof
curl localhost:9090/debug/pprof/profile > /tmp/pprof.pb
```
Trace files: s3://redwood-perf/kv-rotor/1765432100/trace.json

ci-bot: Deployed test job redwood/perf/kv-rotor/1765432100 to staging at 2024-11-27T14:02:31Z :white_check_mark:

Tara S: Quick mitigation idea: make merge path lock-free for the common-case (single-fragment) and defer heavy coalescing to background reclaim. Could also add per-batch budget so merges that take > X ms get paused and resumed asynchronously to avoid HOL.

Maria L: +1 to background coalescing. Also maybe change continuous-batching merge heuristic: don't merge a long-context head into a batch of short ones unless they are same shard affinity. Keeps short requests fast.

Josh P: Another angle: prioritize eviction of stale fragments in hot shard via adaptive aging. If a shard grows > threshold we trigger async compaction. That reduces chain scan during merge.

Kevin R: Tried a quick patch: if merged_batch.max_ctx_length > 2048, skip immediate coalesce and instead mark fragments for bg_compact. Results: HOL events drop ~80% in short-request tail in staging run. Memory still grows slower but manageable.

Tara S: Nice. Can you paste the diff or config toggle?

Kevin R: Patch (conceptual):
```
if merged_batch.max_ctx_length > config.merge_short_long_threshold {
  mark_for_bg_compact(shard);
  continue; // skip sync coalesce
}
```
Config knob: merge_short_long_threshold=2048 (default unset => old behavior).

Maria L: Need tests: simulate race where bg_compact runs concurrently with reclaim. Also make sure we don't leak references if we postpone coalesce.

Kevin R: Agreed. I'll add unit tests around fragment refcounts + one e2e perf job.

Josh P: Also add metric: "kv.merge_skipped_due_to_long_ctx" and a gauge for "shard_fragment_chain_len" so we can alert before it hits pathological values.

ci-bot: Metric rule created: alerts/kv-fragment-chain-high (warn at chain_len>500) by Josh P

Tara S: We should also audit the kernel selection path to ensure we don't accidentally change eviction timing because of different token throughput (faster kernels may keep slices alive longer due to different latencies). But since Kevin said both kernels reproduce, lower priority.

Kevin R: Follow-ups: I'll land the feature-flagged skip-coalesce patch to a branch, add tests, run 3-hour soak with mixed traffic. If stable, flip config on canary.

Maria L: Thx. Also add a small doc blurb in eng-runtime/ops playbook for when to toggle merge_short_long_threshold for specific customers (long-context heavy).

Kevin R: Will do. Tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.

Josh P: If you want me to run extended perf, ping me.

Kevin R: Thanks — will ping when the branch is ready. :thumbsup:
